case.question: Houthis enter Aden by December 31, 2026?
case.literal_rule: YES for deliberate Houthi military operation within any part of seven named districts: Craiter/Sirah, At Tawahi, Al Mualla, Khur Maksar, Ash Shaikh Outhman, Dar Sad, Al Mansura. Al Buraiqeh/Little Aden alone excluded. Bombardment, sabotage, offshore naval presence, threats/claims alone, emissaries, or POW status do not suffice. Genuine ambiguity may keep market open 3 days after deadline. Resolution source is consensus of credible reporting.

current_official_context.reported: UN Special Envoy said hostilities had spread across multiple fronts; fighting continued west/south of Taiz and across into Lahj; government had reported retaking areas around Bab al-Mandab. This account does not report Houthi ground entry into any named Aden district.

relevant_ground_incursion_lead.reported: RTÉ relayed an unnamed internationally-recognized-government military official saying armed Houthi fighters reached Mayyun/Perim Island after government forces withdrew the previous day and the group had taken it. This is a reported ground landing after market creation, but Mayyun’s relationship to the rule’s seven exact districts is not established by this source.

later_status_and_aden_attacks.source: Anaween Center Yemen interactive map, https://anaweencenter.org/en/map
later_status_and_aden_attacks.observed: Search result displayed a provisional assessment dated 2026-10-15 stating Mayyun was government-controlled and belonged administratively to Aden; direct HTML GET 200 was captured but the map/status text was not present in its static HTML, so this statement is search-index evidence only and its exact administrative boundary claim is unverified here.
later_status_and_aden_attacks.other_source: AP story https://apnews.com/article/c39ea48032c0e8a76558b0296bb25244 (search result dated 2026-10-16) reported two missiles hitting Aden airport and attributed blame to police; direct GET returned 403, body preserved at logs/deep_review_20261017/case0396_facts_1745/ap_aden_airport.body.json.gz, status/body SHA in receipt. Missile attack alone is expressly nonqualifying. AP search result dated 2026-10-15 also reported Houthi-claimed explosions near a government palace in Aden, but this is not evidence of ground entry.

material_unknowns: The September Mayyun landing is not geospatially tied here to one of the seven named districts; reporting that it belongs to Aden Governorate does not by itself establish a named district. Current district control remains uncertain in available bounded sources.

The UN Oct9 account concerns adjacent fronts and government-reported recaptures around Bab al-Mandab, not an exact Aden-district operation. AP’s later Aden stories describe missile/explosion attacks, which the frozen rule excludes absent ground entry.
No comprehensive post-creation incident log or district-level map was verified. Bounded lack of a qualifying report is not proof none occurred.
source_scope: Facts only; no probability, quote, or resolution judgment.
